action: POSTECH account holders: change the unified account password (and anywhere it was reused) and watch for phishing that uses your ID or email, following the university's notice.
exec: A South Korean university reports a leak of 19,978 records from two campus portals; no national ID numbers are reported leaked.
org: POSTECH (Pohang University of Science and Technology)
plain: POSTECH in South Korea says hackers broke into two campus portals and 19,978 records of account IDs and other details leaked. The university says no national ID, passport or driver's licence numbers were leaked so far.
summary: According to Dailysecu, POSTECH posted a notice on 19 November that attackers used security flaws in its research equipment portal (RETINA) and IT service portal (HEMOS) to gain administrator privileges. The notice reports 19,978 records leaked: 19,500 account IDs with encrypted passwords and 478 IDs with emails and affiliations. The attack was found after an illegal mining program turned up on a lab GPU server.
title: POSTECH says portal hack leaked 19,978 records; illegal mining program found on lab GPU server

validation.note: Single publisher (Dailysecu) relaying the university's own notice; the notice itself was not read.

review.note: Checked 19,978 = 19,500 + 478, RETINA/HEMOS, admin privileges, mining program, no ID numbers leaked, 19 Nov notice against Dailysecu
